324	def _validate_submit_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
325	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str], dict[str, dict[str, str]]
326	]:
327	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_ROOT_FIELDS):
328	        raise ValueError("acceptance file root must be an object with keys "
329	                         "version, jobs, idempotency and audit")
330	
331	    version = data["version"]
332	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _SUBMIT_VERSION:
333	        raise ValueError("unsupported acceptance file version")
334	
335	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
336	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
337	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
338	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) \
339	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
340	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
341	        raise ValueError("jobs, idempotency and audit must be objects")
342	    _check_sorted_keys(jobs_raw, "jobs")
343	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
344	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
345	
346	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
347	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
348	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
349	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
350	        if not isinstance(record, dict) \
351	                or set(record.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS):
352	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
353	        if record["job_id"] != name or not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
354	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
355	        if not _is_plain_int(record["work"]) or record["work"] <= 0:
356	            raise ValueError("invalid work")
357	        for field in ("deadline", "max_cost", "carbon_cap"):
358	            if not _is_plain_int(record[field]) or record[field] < 0:
359	                raise ValueError(f"invalid {field}")
360	        regions = _validate_region_field(record["regions"], "regions")
361	        residency = _validate_region_field(record["residency"], "residency")
362	        if not set(residency).issubset(regions):
363	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be a subset of regions")
364	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
365	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
366	        jobs[name] = {field: record[field] for field in _SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS}
367	
368	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
369	    referenced: set[str] = set()
370	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
371	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
372	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
373	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
374	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference an accepted "
375	                             "job")
376	        if job_id in referenced:
377	            raise ValueError("job accepted under more than one idempotency "
378	                             "key")
379	        referenced.add(job_id)
380	        idempotency[key] = job_id
381	
382	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
383	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
384	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
385	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
386	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
387	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_EVENT_FIELDS):
388	            raise ValueError("submit audit event has invalid fields")
389	        event_key = event["key"]
390	        job_id = event["job_id"]
391	        result = event["result"]
392	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
393	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
394	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
395	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference an accepted job")
396	        if result != _STATE:
397	            raise ValueError("audit event result must be queued")
398	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "job_id": job_id,
399	                       "result": result}
400	
401	    # The three sections describe one acceptance history: each
402	    # idempotency key binds one job and one submit event, every accepted
403	    # job has both, and the event and the map agree on the job.
404	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
405	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
406	    for key, job_id in idempotency.items():
407	        if events[key]["job_id"] != job_id:
408	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
409	                             "entry")
410	    if set(jobs) != referenced:
411	        raise ValueError("every accepted job must be bound to an "
412	                         "idempotency key")
413	
414	    return jobs, idempotency, events

417	def _load_submit_file(
418	    realpath: str,
419	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str],
420	           dict[str, dict[str, str]], bytes | None]:
421	    try:
422	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
423	            raw = handle.read()
424	    except FileNotFoundError:
425	        return {}, {}, {}, None
426	
427	    try:
428	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
429	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
430	        raise ValueError(
431	            f"acceptance file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
432	    try:
433	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
434	        data = finite_loads(text)
435	    except ValueError as exc:
436	        raise ValueError(
437	            f"acceptance file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
438	    jobs, idempotency, events = _validate_submit_structure(data)
439	    return jobs, idempotency, events, raw

442	def _serialize_submit_file(
443	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
444	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
445	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
446	) -> bytes:
447	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
448	    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
449	    payload = {
450	        "version": _SUBMIT_VERSION,
451	        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
452	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
453	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
454	    }
455	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
456	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
457	    return text.encode("utf-8")

460	def _rollback_submit_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
461	                          old_bytes: bytes | None,
462	                          first: BaseException) -> None:
463	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
464	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
465	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
466	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
467	    try:
468	        if old_bytes is None:
469	            try:
470	                os.unlink(realpath)
471	            except FileNotFoundError:
472	                pass
473	        else:
474	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
475	                dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
476	            try:
477	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
478	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
479	                    handle.flush()
480	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
481	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
482	            except BaseException:
483	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
484	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
485	                raise
486	        _fsync_directory(directory)
487	    except OSError as recovery:
488	        raise recovery from first
489	
490	
491	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
492	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
493	    try:
494	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
495	    finally:
496	        os.close(dir_fd)
497	
498	
499	def _commit_submit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
500	                        old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
501	    # One durable commit for jobs, the idempotency map and the audit
502	    # event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
503	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
504	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful submit leaves the original file
505	    # byte-for-byte.
506	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
507	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
508	        dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-submit-", suffix=".tmp")
509	    try:
510	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
511	            handle.write(payload)
512	            handle.flush()
513	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
514	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
515	    except BaseException as first:
516	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
517	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
518	        raise
519	    try:
520	        _fsync_directory(directory)
521	    except BaseException as first:
522	        _rollback_submit_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
523	        raise

526	def submit(path: str, job: dict[str, object], idempotency_key: str
527	           ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
528	    """Persistently accept a complete scheduling-constraint job.
529	
530	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The job
531	    must be an object with exactly the seven top-level fields job_id,
532	    work, deadline, regions, residency, max_cost and carbon_cap: a
533	    non-empty id, a positive work amount, non-negative deadline,
534	    max_cost and carbon_cap (booleans rejected), and two non-empty lists
535	    of distinct non-empty region strings, residency a subset of regions.
536	    Any deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
537	
538	    A first acceptance saves the canonical job -- both region lists
539	    sorted by code point, state ``"queued"`` -- together with the
540	    idempotency binding and a submit audit event carrying the key, the
541	    job id and the queued result, all three in one durable commit, and
542	    returns ``(record, True)``. Replaying the same key with an
543	    equivalent job returns the stored record with ``False`` without
544	    adding an event or rewriting the file; the same key with a different
545	    job, an already accepted job id under another key, or any constraint
546	    mismatch raises ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
547	
548	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
549	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
550	    version, structure, ordering or references) raises ``ValueError``;
551	    any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Calls serialize
552	    across threads and processes per resolved real path.
553	    """
554	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
555	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
556	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
557	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
558	    record = _normalize_submit_job(job)
559	    job_id = record["job_id"]
560	
561	    store = _get_store(path)
562	    with store.lock:
563	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
564	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
565	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
566	            jobs, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_submit_file(
567	                store.realpath)
568	
569	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
570	            if existing_id is not None:
571	                existing = jobs[existing_id]
572	                if existing != record:
573	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
574	                                     "a different job")
575	                return dict(existing), False
576	
577	            if job_id in jobs:
578	                raise ValueError("job_id is already accepted under another "
579	                                 "idempotency key")
580	
581	            jobs[job_id] = record
582	            idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
583	            events[idempotency_key] = {
584	                "key": idempotency_key,
585	                "job_id": job_id,
586	                "result": _STATE,
587	            }
588	            _commit_submit_file(
589	                store.realpath,
590	                _serialize_submit_file(jobs, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
591	            return dict(record), True
592

594	def get(path: str, job_id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
595	    """Return a read-only copy of the accepted job stored under ``job_id``.
596	
597	    ``path`` and ``job_id`` must be non-empty strings, else
598	    ``ValueError``. A missing acceptance file raises
599	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including a version-1
600	    ``jobs.register`` file, which is never upgraded -- raises
601	    ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises ``KeyError(job_id)``; any
602	    other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. The call never
603	    writes, and the returned record is a fresh copy with job_id, work,
604	    deadline, regions, residency, max_cost, carbon_cap and state.
605	    """
606	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
607	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
608	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
609	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
610	
611	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
612	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
613	        jobs, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_submit_file(realpath)
614	    if raw is None:
615	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"acceptance file {realpath!r} does not exist")
616	    if job_id not in jobs:
617	        raise KeyError(job_id)
618	    return dict(jobs[job_id])

1	"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process resource-supply registry.
2	
3	One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
4	market:
5	
6	* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
7	  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
8	* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
9	* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
10	  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.
11	
12	Every read entry requires the on-disk document to be exactly the
13	canonical compact form :func:`_serialize` produces -- fields and keys
14	in their fixed/code-point order, no whitespace beyond structural
15	tokens, non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline. Any
16	out-of-order section, extra whitespace, ``\\uXXXX``-escaped non-ASCII
17	character, or missing or duplicated final newline is a ``ValueError``.
18	
19	:func:`publish` appends a new version under an idempotency key,
20	:func:`get` reads one resource record back by id and optional version,
21	and :func:`feasible` joins a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file with the
22	supply file under both shared locks to rank the resources that can
23	serve one accepted job at an evaluation moment. The supply file is
24	never rewritten by the read paths, and a version-1 ``jobs.register``
25	file is not a supply file.
26	
27	The persistence machinery -- per-real-path mutexes, the companion
28	flock, canonical loading and the durable atomic commit with rollback --
29	is the shared infrastructure of :mod:`carbon_market._lifecycle`; this
30	module keeps only the supply ledger's own format, validation and
31	wording.
32	"""
33	
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import contextlib
37	import json
38	import os
39	from typing import Any
40	
41	from . import _lifecycle
42	from . import jobs as _jobs
43	from . import signals as _signals

45	__all__ = ["publish", "get", "feasible", "feasible_live"]

48	_RESOURCE_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "region", "capacity", "start", "end",
49	                    "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
50	_RECORD_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version", "region", "capacity", "start",
51	                  "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")

64	def _check_values(resource: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
65	    region = resource["region"]
66	    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
67	        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
68	
69	    capacity = resource["capacity"]
70	    if not _is_plain_int(capacity) or capacity <= 0:
71	        raise ValueError("capacity must be a non-boolean positive integer")
72	
73	    for name in ("start", "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
74	        value = resource[name]
75	        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
76	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
77	                             "integer")
78	    if resource["start"] > resource["end"]:
79	        raise ValueError("start must not be later than end")
80	
81	    residency = resource["residency"]
82	    if not isinstance(residency, list) or not residency:
83	        raise ValueError("residency must be a non-empty list")
84	    seen: set[str] = set()
85	    for entry in residency:
86	        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry:
87	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
88	        if entry in seen:
89	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
90	        seen.add(entry)
91	    # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
92	    if residency != sorted(residency):
93	        raise ValueError("residency regions must be sorted by code point")
94	    if region not in seen:
95	        raise ValueError("residency regions must contain the resource region")

124	def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
125	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
126	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
127	]:
128	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
129	        raise ValueError("supply file root must be an object with keys "
130	                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")
131	
132	    version = data["version"]
133	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
134	        raise ValueError("unsupported supply file version")
135	
136	    history_raw = data["history"]
137	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
138	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
139	    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
140	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
141	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
142	        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
143	    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
144	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
145	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
146	
147	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
148	    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
149	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
150	            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
151	        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
152	            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
153	                             "per resource")
154	        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
155	        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
156	            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
157	                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
158	                raise ValueError("resource record has invalid fields")
159	            if record["resource_id"] != resource_id:
160	                raise ValueError("resource record id does not match its key")
161	            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
162	                    or record["version"] != index:
163	                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
164	            _check_values(record)
165	            if records and record["start"] <= records[-1]["start"]:
166	                raise ValueError("resource starts must increase across "
167	                                 "versions")
168	            records.append({
169	                "resource_id": resource_id,
170	                "version": index,
171	                "region": record["region"],
172	                "capacity": record["capacity"],
173	                "start": record["start"],
174	                "end": record["end"],
175	                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
176	                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
177	                "residency": list(record["residency"]),
178	            })
179	        history[resource_id] = records
180	
181	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
182	    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():
183	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
184	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
185	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
186	                or resource_id not in history:
187	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
188	                             "resource")
189	        idempotency[key] = resource_id
190	
191	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
192	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
193	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
194	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
195	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
196	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
197	            raise ValueError("publish audit event has invalid fields")
198	        event_key = event["key"]
199	        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
200	        event_version = event["version"]
201	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
202	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
203	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
204	                or resource_id not in history:
205	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
206	                             "resource")
207	        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
208	                or event_version > len(history[resource_id]):
209	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
210	                             "version")
211	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "resource_id": resource_id,
212	                       "version": event_version}
213	
214	    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
215	    # idempotency key binds one resource and one publish event, the map
216	    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version
217	    # is bound to exactly one event.
218	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
219	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
220	    for key, resource_id in idempotency.items():
221	        if events[key]["resource_id"] != resource_id:
222	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
223	                             "entry")
224	    published = {(resource_id, record["version"])
225	                 for resource_id, records in history.items()
226	                 for record in records}
227	    bound = {(event["resource_id"], event["version"])
228	             for event in events.values()}
229	    if bound != published:
230	        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
231	                         "audit event")
232	
233	    return history, idempotency, events

236	def _canonical_bytes(
237	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
238	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
239	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
240	) -> bytes:
241	    # The canonical wire form every reader accepts: compact UTF-8 JSON
242	    # with non-ASCII written through, sections in their fixed field order
243	    # and each section's primary keys in code-point order, terminated by
244	    # exactly one newline. The round trip also rejects duplicate keys
245	    # (json.loads keeps the last occurrence) and any escaping of
246	    # non-ASCII characters that json.dumps would write through.
247	    return _serialize(history, idempotency, events)
248

250	def _canonical_sections(
251	    sections: tuple[dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
252	                    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]],
253	) -> bytes:
254	    history, idempotency, events = sections
255	    return _canonical_bytes(history, idempotency, events)

258	def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
259	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
260	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
261	]:
262	    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
263	    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
264	    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline. Any
265	    # extra whitespace, escaped non-ASCII character, reordered field or
266	    # missing/duplicated final newline is a ValueError. A missing file
267	    # maps to the empty initial state.
268	    sections, raw = _lifecycle.load_canonical(
269	        realpath, "supply file", _validate_structure, _canonical_sections)
270	    if sections is None:
271	        return {}, {}, {}, None
272	    history, idempotency, events = sections
273	    return history, idempotency, events, raw
274

276	def _serialize(
277	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
278	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
279	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
280	) -> bytes:
281	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
282	    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
283	    payload = {
284	        "version": _VERSION,
285	        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
286	                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
287	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
288	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
289	    }
290	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
291	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
292	    return text.encode("utf-8")
293

295	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
296	    _lifecycle.fsync_directory(directory)
297

299	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
300	                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
301	    _lifecycle.rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first,
302	                             prefix=".resources-restore-",
303	                             fsync_dir=_fsync_directory)
304

306	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
307	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
308	    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
309	    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
310	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
311	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
312	    # byte-for-byte.
313	    _lifecycle.commit_file(realpath, payload, old_bytes,
314	                           prefix=".resources-", fsync_dir=_fsync_directory)
315

317	def publish(
318	    path: str,
319	    resource: dict[str, object],
320	    idempotency_key: str,
321	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
322	    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.
323	
324	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
325	    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
326	    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
327	    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
328	    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
329	    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
330	    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
331	    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
332	    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
333	
334	    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
335	    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
336	    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
337	    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
338	    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
339	    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
340	    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
341	    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
342	    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
343	    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
344	    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
345	
346	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
347	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
348	    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
349	    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
350	    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
351	    """
352	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
353	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
354	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
355	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
356	    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
357	    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]
358	
359	    store = _get_store(path)
360	    with store.lock:
361	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
362	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
363	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
364	            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
365	                store.realpath)
366	
367	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
368	            if existing_id is not None:
369	                event = events[idempotency_key]
370	                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
371	                if {field: existing[field]
372	                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
373	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
374	                                     "a different resource")
375	                return dict(existing), False
376	
377	            versions = history.get(resource_id)
378	            if versions is None:
379	                versions = []
380	                history[resource_id] = versions
381	                version = 1
382	            else:
383	                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
384	                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
385	                                     "versions")
386	                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1
387	
388	            record: dict[str, Any] = {
389	                "resource_id": resource_id,
390	                "version": version,
391	                "region": normalized["region"],
392	                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
393	                "start": normalized["start"],
394	                "end": normalized["end"],
395	                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
396	                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
397	                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
398	            }
399	            versions.append(record)
400	            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
401	            events[idempotency_key] = {
402	                "key": idempotency_key,
403	                "resource_id": resource_id,
404	                "version": version,
405	            }
406	            _commit_file(store.realpath,
407	                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
408	            return dict(record), True
409	
410	
411	def get(
412	    path: str,
413	    resource_id: str,
414	    version: int | None = None,
415	) -> dict[str, object]:
416	    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.
417	
418	    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
419	    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
420	    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
421	    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
422	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
423	    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown resource id raises
424	    ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown version
425	    ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
426	    ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record is a
427	    fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start, end,
428	    unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
429	    """
430	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
431	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
432	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
433	        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
434	    if version is not None \
435	            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
436	        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")
437	
438	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
439	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
440	        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
441	    if raw is None:
442	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
443	    versions = history.get(resource_id)
444	    if versions is None:
445	        raise KeyError(resource_id)
446	    if version is None:
447	        return dict(versions[-1])
448	    if version > len(versions):
449	        raise KeyError(version)
450	    return dict(versions[version - 1])
451	
452	def feasible(
453	    job_path: str,
454	    supply_path: str,
455	    job_id: str,
456	    at: int,
457	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
458	    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.
459	
460	    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
461	    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
462	    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
463	    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
464	    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
465	    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.
466	
467	    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
468	    an invalid file -- including a supply file outside canonical
469	    compact form -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
470	    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
471	    ``OSError``.
472	
473	    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
474	    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
475	    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
476	    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
477	    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
478	    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
479	    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
480	    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
481	    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
482	    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
483	    candidate the list is empty.
484	    """
485	    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
486	        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
487	    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
488	        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
489	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
490	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
491	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
492	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
493	
494	    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
495	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
496	    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
497	    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
498	    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
499	        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
500	            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))
501	
502	        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
503	            job_real)
504	        if job_raw is None:
505	            raise FileNotFoundError(
506	                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
507	        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
508	        if supply_raw is None:
509	            raise FileNotFoundError(
510	                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
511	
512	        job = accepted.get(job_id)
513	        if job is None:
514	            raise KeyError(job_id)
515	
516	        work = job["work"]
517	        regions = set(job["regions"])
518	        residency = set(job["residency"])
519	        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
520	        for records in history.values():
521	            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
522	            for record in records:
523	                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
524	                    active = record
525	            if active is None:
526	                continue
527	            if active["region"] not in regions:
528	                continue
529	            if active["capacity"] < work:
530	                continue
531	            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
532	                continue
533	            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
534	                continue
535	            total_cost = work * active["unit_cost"]
536	            total_carbon = work * active["carbon_intensity"]
537	            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
538	                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
539	                continue
540	            candidates.append({
541	                "resource": dict(active),
542	                "total_cost": total_cost,
543	                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
544	            })
545	
546	    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (entry["resource"]["carbon_intensity"],
547	                                       entry["resource"]["unit_cost"],
548	                                       entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
549	    return candidates
550	
551	
552	def feasible_live(
553	    job_path: str,
554	    supply_path: str,
555	    signal_path: str,
556	    job_id: str,
557	    at: int,
558	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
559	    """Rank resources for one accepted job at ``at`` against live signals.
560	
561	    This is the dynamic counterpart of :func:`feasible`: the
562	    ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the supply file and the live signal
563	    file are read as one snapshot while their shared locks are held
564	    together. ``job_path``, ``supply_path`` and ``signal_path`` must be
565	    non-empty strings (and resolve to distinct real locations),
566	    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
567	    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``.
568	
569	    As in :func:`feasible`, each resource contributes only its highest
570	    supply version valid at ``at`` and must sit in one of the job's
571	    regions, offer at least the job's work as capacity, cover the job's
572	    residency regions and stay available at least until the job's
573	    deadline. Instead of the version's static figures, the unit cost and
574	    carbon intensity are taken from the resource region's latest signal
575	    observed no later than ``at`` and not expired at it; a resource
576	    whose region has no valid signal at ``at`` is simply excluded. The
577	    total cost is the job's work times the signal unit cost and the
578	    total carbon the work times the signal carbon intensity, with the
579	    same max_cost and carbon_cap budget exclusions as :func:`feasible`.
580	
581	    The result is ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit
582	    cost, then resource id; each entry carries the resource record, the
583	    signal record (including its version) and both totals --
584	    ``resource``, ``signal``, ``total_cost`` and ``total_carbon`` in that
585	    order -- and is an empty list when nothing qualifies.
586	
587	    A missing acceptance, supply or signal file raises
588	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
589	    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
590	    ``KeyError(job_id)``; the absence of a valid signal is never an
591	    error, it only removes the resource; any other locking or I/O
592	    failure raises ``OSError``.
593	    """
594	    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
595	        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
596	    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
597	        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
598	    if not isinstance(signal_path, str) or not signal_path:
599	        raise ValueError("signal_path must be a non-empty string")
600	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
601	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
602	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
603	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
604	
605	    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
606	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
607	    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signal_path)
608	    if len({job_real, supply_real, signal_real}) != 3:
609	        raise ValueError("job, supply and signal paths must be distinct "
610	                         "real paths")
611	
612	    # Lock all three snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
613	    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
614	    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
615	        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real, signal_real}):
616	            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))
617	
618	        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
619	            job_real)
620	        if job_raw is None:
621	            raise FileNotFoundError(
622	                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
623	        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
624	        if supply_raw is None:
625	            raise FileNotFoundError(
626	                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
627	        signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
628	            _signals._load_file(signal_real)
629	        if signal_raw is None:
630	            raise FileNotFoundError(
631	                f"signal file {signal_real!r} does not exist")
632	
633	        job = accepted.get(job_id)
634	        if job is None:
635	            raise KeyError(job_id)
636	
637	        work = job["work"]
638	        regions = set(job["regions"])
639	        residency = set(job["residency"])
640	        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
641	        for records in history.values():
642	            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
643	            for record in records:
644	                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
645	                    active = record
646	            if active is None:
647	                continue
648	            if active["region"] not in regions:
649	                continue
650	            if active["capacity"] < work:
651	                continue
652	            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
653	                continue
654	            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
655	                continue
656	            # The live signal drives both figures; a region without a
657	            # current signal contributes no candidate.
658	            signal = None
659	            for signal_record in signal_history.get(active["region"], ()):
660	                if signal_record["observed"] <= at <= signal_record["expires"]:
661	                    signal = signal_record
662	            if signal is None:
663	                continue
664	            total_cost = work * signal["unit_cost"]
665	            total_carbon = work * signal["carbon_intensity"]
666	            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
667	                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
668	                continue
669	            signal_copy = dict(signal)
670	            signal_copy["mix"] = dict(signal["mix"])
671	            candidates.append({
672	                "resource": dict(active),
673	                "signal": signal_copy,
674	                "total_cost": total_cost,
675	                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
676	            })
677	
678	    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (
679	        entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
680	        entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
681	        entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
682	    return candidates

"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process resource-supply registry.

One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
market:

* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.

Every read entry requires the on-disk document to be exactly the
canonical compact form :func:`_serialize` produces -- fields and keys
in their fixed/code-point order, no whitespace beyond structural
tokens, non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline. Any
out-of-order section, extra whitespace, ``\\uXXXX``-escaped non-ASCII
character, or missing or duplicated final newline is a ``ValueError``.

:func:`publish` appends a new version under an idempotency key,
:func:`get` reads one resource record back by id and optional version,
and :func:`feasible` joins a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file with the
supply file under both shared locks to rank the resources that can
serve one accepted job at an evaluation moment. The supply file is
never rewritten by the read paths, and a version-1 ``jobs.register``
file is not a supply file.

The persistence machinery -- per-real-path mutexes, the companion
flock, canonical loading and the durable atomic commit with rollback --
is the shared infrastructure of :mod:`carbon_market._lifecycle`; this
module keeps only the supply ledger's own format, validation and
wording.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import json
import os
from typing import Any

from . import _lifecycle
from . import jobs as _jobs
from . import signals as _signals

__all__ = ["publish", "get", "feasible", "feasible_live"]

_VERSION = 1
_RESOURCE_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "region", "capacity", "start", "end",
                    "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
_RECORD_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version", "region", "capacity", "start",
                  "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "history", "idempotency", "audit")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "resource_id", "version")

# The shared persistence infrastructure, bound to this module's names so
# existing callers and fault-injection seams keep working.
_Store = _lifecycle.Store
_get_store = _lifecycle.get_store
_is_plain_int = _lifecycle.is_plain_int
_check_sorted_keys = _lifecycle.check_sorted_keys
_process_lock = _lifecycle.file_lock


def _check_values(resource: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    region = resource["region"]
    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")

    capacity = resource["capacity"]
    if not _is_plain_int(capacity) or capacity <= 0:
        raise ValueError("capacity must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    for name in ("start", "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
        value = resource[name]
        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
                             "integer")
    if resource["start"] > resource["end"]:
        raise ValueError("start must not be later than end")

    residency = resource["residency"]
    if not isinstance(residency, list) or not residency:
        raise ValueError("residency must be a non-empty list")
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for entry in residency:
        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry:
            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
        if entry in seen:
            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
        seen.add(entry)
    # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
    if residency != sorted(residency):
        raise ValueError("residency regions must be sorted by code point")
    if region not in seen:
        raise ValueError("residency regions must contain the resource region")


def _normalize_resource(resource: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_RESOURCE_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("resource must be an object with exactly "
                         "resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, "
                         "unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency")

    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")

    normalized: dict[str, Any] = {
        "resource_id": resource_id,
        "region": resource["region"],
        "capacity": resource["capacity"],
        "start": resource["start"],
        "end": resource["end"],
        "unit_cost": resource["unit_cost"],
        "carbon_intensity": resource["carbon_intensity"],
        "residency": resource["residency"],
    }
    _check_values(normalized)
    normalized["residency"] = list(normalized["residency"])
    return normalized


def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("supply file root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported supply file version")

    history_raw = data["history"]
    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
    audit_raw = data["audit"]
    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")

    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
                             "per resource")
        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
                raise ValueError("resource record has invalid fields")
            if record["resource_id"] != resource_id:
                raise ValueError("resource record id does not match its key")
            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
                    or record["version"] != index:
                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
            _check_values(record)
            if records and record["start"] <= records[-1]["start"]:
                raise ValueError("resource starts must increase across "
                                 "versions")
            records.append({
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": index,
                "region": record["region"],
                "capacity": record["capacity"],
                "start": record["start"],
                "end": record["end"],
                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(record["residency"]),
            })
        history[resource_id] = records

    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
                or resource_id not in history:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
                             "resource")
        idempotency[key] = resource_id

    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("publish audit event has invalid fields")
        event_key = event["key"]
        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
        event_version = event["version"]
        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
                or resource_id not in history:
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
                             "resource")
        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
                or event_version > len(history[resource_id]):
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
                             "version")
        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "resource_id": resource_id,
                       "version": event_version}

    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
    # idempotency key binds one resource and one publish event, the map
    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version
    # is bound to exactly one event.
    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
    for key, resource_id in idempotency.items():
        if events[key]["resource_id"] != resource_id:
            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
                             "entry")
    published = {(resource_id, record["version"])
                 for resource_id, records in history.items()
                 for record in records}
    bound = {(event["resource_id"], event["version"])
             for event in events.values()}
    if bound != published:
        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
                         "audit event")

    return history, idempotency, events


def _canonical_bytes(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # The canonical wire form every reader accepts: compact UTF-8 JSON
    # with non-ASCII written through, sections in their fixed field order
    # and each section's primary keys in code-point order, terminated by
    # exactly one newline. The round trip also rejects duplicate keys
    # (json.loads keeps the last occurrence) and any escaping of
    # non-ASCII characters that json.dumps would write through.
    return _serialize(history, idempotency, events)


def _canonical_sections(
    sections: tuple[dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
                    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]],
) -> bytes:
    history, idempotency, events = sections
    return _canonical_bytes(history, idempotency, events)


def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
]:
    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline. Any
    # extra whitespace, escaped non-ASCII character, reordered field or
    # missing/duplicated final newline is a ValueError. A missing file
    # maps to the empty initial state.
    sections, raw = _lifecycle.load_canonical(
        realpath, "supply file", _validate_structure, _canonical_sections)
    if sections is None:
        return {}, {}, {}, None
    history, idempotency, events = sections
    return history, idempotency, events, raw


def _serialize(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    _lifecycle.fsync_directory(directory)


def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
    _lifecycle.rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first,
                             prefix=".resources-restore-",
                             fsync_dir=_fsync_directory)


def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
    # byte-for-byte.
    _lifecycle.commit_file(realpath, payload, old_bytes,
                           prefix=".resources-", fsync_dir=_fsync_directory)


def publish(
    path: str,
    resource: dict[str, object],
    idempotency_key: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.

    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.

    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.

    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
                store.realpath)

            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
            if existing_id is not None:
                event = events[idempotency_key]
                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
                if {field: existing[field]
                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different resource")
                return dict(existing), False

            versions = history.get(resource_id)
            if versions is None:
                versions = []
                history[resource_id] = versions
                version = 1
            else:
                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
                                     "versions")
                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1

            record: dict[str, Any] = {
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
                "region": normalized["region"],
                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
                "start": normalized["start"],
                "end": normalized["end"],
                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
            }
            versions.append(record)
            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
            events[idempotency_key] = {
                "key": idempotency_key,
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
            }
            _commit_file(store.realpath,
                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
            return dict(record), True


def get(
    path: str,
    resource_id: str,
    version: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.

    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown resource id raises
    ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown version
    ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record is a
    fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start, end,
    unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
    if version is not None \
            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
    if raw is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
    versions = history.get(resource_id)
    if versions is None:
        raise KeyError(resource_id)
    if version is None:
        return dict(versions[-1])
    if version > len(versions):
        raise KeyError(version)
    return dict(versions[version - 1])

def feasible(
    job_path: str,
    supply_path: str,
    job_id: str,
    at: int,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.

    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.

    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
    an invalid file -- including a supply file outside canonical
    compact form -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``.

    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
    candidate the list is empty.
    """
    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))

        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
            job_real)
        if job_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
        if supply_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")

        job = accepted.get(job_id)
        if job is None:
            raise KeyError(job_id)

        work = job["work"]
        regions = set(job["regions"])
        residency = set(job["residency"])
        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for records in history.values():
            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
            for record in records:
                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
                    active = record
            if active is None:
                continue
            if active["region"] not in regions:
                continue
            if active["capacity"] < work:
                continue
            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
                continue
            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
                continue
            total_cost = work * active["unit_cost"]
            total_carbon = work * active["carbon_intensity"]
            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
                continue
            candidates.append({
                "resource": dict(active),
                "total_cost": total_cost,
                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
            })

    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (entry["resource"]["carbon_intensity"],
                                       entry["resource"]["unit_cost"],
                                       entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
    return candidates


def feasible_live(
    job_path: str,
    supply_path: str,
    signal_path: str,
    job_id: str,
    at: int,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Rank resources for one accepted job at ``at`` against live signals.

    This is the dynamic counterpart of :func:`feasible`: the
    ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the supply file and the live signal
    file are read as one snapshot while their shared locks are held
    together. ``job_path``, ``supply_path`` and ``signal_path`` must be
    non-empty strings (and resolve to distinct real locations),
    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``.

    As in :func:`feasible`, each resource contributes only its highest
    supply version valid at ``at`` and must sit in one of the job's
    regions, offer at least the job's work as capacity, cover the job's
    residency regions and stay available at least until the job's
    deadline. Instead of the version's static figures, the unit cost and
    carbon intensity are taken from the resource region's latest signal
    observed no later than ``at`` and not expired at it; a resource
    whose region has no valid signal at ``at`` is simply excluded. The
    total cost is the job's work times the signal unit cost and the
    total carbon the work times the signal carbon intensity, with the
    same max_cost and carbon_cap budget exclusions as :func:`feasible`.

    The result is ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit
    cost, then resource id; each entry carries the resource record, the
    signal record (including its version) and both totals --
    ``resource``, ``signal``, ``total_cost`` and ``total_carbon`` in that
    order -- and is an empty list when nothing qualifies.

    A missing acceptance, supply or signal file raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
    ``KeyError(job_id)``; the absence of a valid signal is never an
    error, it only removes the resource; any other locking or I/O
    failure raises ``OSError``.
    """
    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(signal_path, str) or not signal_path:
        raise ValueError("signal_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signal_path)
    if len({job_real, supply_real, signal_real}) != 3:
        raise ValueError("job, supply and signal paths must be distinct "
                         "real paths")

    # Lock all three snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real, signal_real}):
            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))

        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
            job_real)
        if job_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
        if supply_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
        signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
            _signals._load_file(signal_real)
        if signal_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"signal file {signal_real!r} does not exist")

        job = accepted.get(job_id)
        if job is None:
            raise KeyError(job_id)

        work = job["work"]
        regions = set(job["regions"])
        residency = set(job["residency"])
        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for records in history.values():
            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
            for record in records:
                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
                    active = record
            if active is None:
                continue
            if active["region"] not in regions:
                continue
            if active["capacity"] < work:
                continue
            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
                continue
            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
                continue
            # The live signal drives both figures; a region without a
            # current signal contributes no candidate.
            signal = None
            for signal_record in signal_history.get(active["region"], ()):
                if signal_record["observed"] <= at <= signal_record["expires"]:
                    signal = signal_record
            if signal is None:
                continue
            total_cost = work * signal["unit_cost"]
            total_carbon = work * signal["carbon_intensity"]
            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
                continue
            signal_copy = dict(signal)
            signal_copy["mix"] = dict(signal["mix"])
            candidates.append({
                "resource": dict(active),
                "signal": signal_copy,
                "total_cost": total_cost,
                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
            })

    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (
        entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
        entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
        entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
    return candidates
